reading.body:
Google has not published the power capacity or square footage of NBY-4 as an individual building. Google's policy is to disclose only aggregate investment figures at the state level, not facility-specific specifications. This campus cannot be sized from public information.

NBY-4 is part of a multi-county Google data center campus spanning Franklin, Licking, and Fairfield counties near Columbus, Ohio. Google's combined announcement of $1.7 billion in investment across new Columbus and Lancaster facilities places it alongside AWS and Meta as a major hyperscale investor in the New Albany and Licking County corridor. The state of Ohio has 76 mapped data center facilities, but only eight operators publish power capacity figures, totaling 60.4 MW of disclosed capacity across the state.

Without published specifications for NBY-4, its significance to AI scaling cannot be assessed from operator disclosures alone. The facility's role in Google's Ohio footprint is real but opaque. Readers tracking grid constraints on AI expansion in Ohio will find Google's aggregate regional investment figures in public record but cannot rank individual Google buildings against competitors or estimate when they will draw power.
